units.own_text: TideGauge stores harbour water-level observations from fixed stations. These rules apply to live station feeds; survey imports are a different service.

Receivers authenticate station messages, a journal preserves arrival order, and an exporter publishes daily bundles. The journal and exporter can restart independently. The dashboard is a read-only consumer and cannot acknowledge observations.

Operational detail is in [Replay](operations.md#replay), [Storage](storage.md#retention), and [Display](dashboard.md#display). These links are a navigation index, not a request to execute every procedure.

These procedures apply only to authenticated live station feeds in the active harbour.

For orientation, the operator console links to the dashboard's [display settings](dashboard.md#display).

To replay an interrupted feed, pause the receiver and obtain a journal checkpoint before requesting the missing interval. Preserve the original observation identifiers during replay. Resume the receiver only after the exporter acknowledges the checkpoint. See the [retention rule](storage.md#retention) before removing journal files.

If a station is still disconnected, do not resume its receiver after replay; leave it paused until a fresh authenticated heartbeat arrives. This exception applies even when the exporter acknowledged the checkpoint.

Survey imports assign new identifiers and may start without a station heartbeat. They are scheduled offline and do not repair a live feed. Reusing this process for a station would create duplicate observations.
Journal files contain original live observations. Exported bundles are derived products, not journal replacements until their checksums have been verified.

Keep a journal file for at least seven days and until the corresponding export checksum is verified. Both conditions must hold before deletion. A legal hold blocks deletion regardless of age or checksum status.
The capacity monitor reports filesystem free space every minute. A low-space alert pauses new survey imports; it does not shorten journal retention or remove a legal hold.
The retired prototype deleted files after two days without checking exports. This behaviour is documented for migration diagnosis and is not the live service policy.
These rules govern daily bundles consumed by harbour analysts.

Publish a bundle only when every included station has a verified daily checksum. Include the observation timezone in the manifest. A missing station must be listed explicitly as missing rather than represented by zero water levels.
A late observation creates a new bundle revision; never overwrite an already published bundle. Keep the previous revision addressable for existing citations.
Preview bundles can omit checksums and use provisional labels. They must stay in the sandbox and are not public daily bundles.
The dashboard presents derived observations and is not a control channel for receivers.

The display rounds water levels to centimetres, highlights delayed stations, and offers a map with a selectable timezone. Hiding a station on the map does not pause its receiver or change export membership.
Browser refresh requests can be repeated freely. They do not replay journal records. Cached display points expire after ten minutes even when original observations remain in storage.
The receiver, journal, exporter and dashboard communicate through durable identifiers.

The append-only journal permits sequential reads and checksum verification. Its file layout groups records by station, while the exporter groups output by civil day. These different groupings explain why a bundle can depend on several files.
The simulator resumes immediately after an in-memory replay and discards records when a demonstration ends. It has no authenticated stations and cannot establish the live receiver recovery policy.
This module-only contract is outside project-only documentation scope.
The survey module calibrates its floating instruments every eighteen hours. This interval does not specify calibration for fixed live stations.

Loom renders museum collection images from preserved camera originals. The production rendering queue is distinct from the interactive preview service.

A manifest binds camera files to object identifiers. Workers produce derivatives, and a publisher exposes approved derivatives to visitors. Re-rendering changes derivatives without changing the preserved camera files.
Workers lease jobs from a shared queue. A lease is a scheduling mechanism, not proof that an output has passed review. The publisher reads the review state separately.
These requirements apply to production derivatives of colour camera originals.

Use the camera profile recorded in the capture manifest, not the worker's default profile. Embed the selected profile identifier in the derivative metadata. If the manifest profile is unavailable, quarantine the job instead of guessing a profile.

For originals explicitly marked monochrome, skip colour conversion but retain the manifest's monochrome marker in derivative metadata. A filename containing the word grey is not sufficient to establish that status.
The preview screen lets an operator choose a temporary display profile. That choice affects only the screen and must not replace the capture manifest profile.
This document governs recovery of production rendering workers after interrupted writes.
Follow all child sections in order when recovering an interrupted worker. A queue retry by itself is not the complete recovery procedure.
Disable the worker lease before inspecting temporary outputs. Preserve the failed job identifier in the incident record.
Compare every completed derivative checksum with its job manifest. Delete only temporary outputs that have no completed manifest entry.
Re-enable the worker lease after checksum validation finishes. Jobs with a checksum mismatch remain quarantined and must not be retried automatically.
Restarting the preview process can discard its entire temporary directory immediately. Preview reset does not apply to production workers or preserved originals.
Publication rules apply to visitor-visible derivatives, not internal previews.

Publish only after both curator approval and checksum verification are recorded. Include the preserved-original identifier with every published derivative. Use the [withdrawal procedure](withdrawal.md#withdrawal) when a published image is recalled.
An active collection embargo prevents publication even after curator approval and checksum verification. Wait for explicit embargo release; reaching a scheduled render date does not release it.
Reviewers may share expiring preview links before approval within the review group. Such links do not make the derivative visitor-visible.
Withdrawal preserves the traceability of images already referenced by visitors.

Replace the public derivative with a withdrawal notice and retain its original identifier. Keep the audit record and preserved camera original. Do not silently redirect the identifier to a different object.
Unpublished draft derivatives can be removed without a public notice. Draft cleanup never removes preserved camera originals.
Loom uses a manifest store, lease queue, raster workers and publication service.

Workers decode tiles, apply transformations and encode derivatives. Tile parallelism reduces memory pressure but does not change the job's approval or embargo state. The pipeline supports several output formats whose encoder implementations are interchangeable.
The demonstration renderer guessed missing camera profiles and published immediately. It was used with disposable sample images and is not a production workflow.
This module-only manual is not included in the project-only operational contract.
The laboratory camera sensor is cleaned with reagent K under the hardware team's procedure. This instruction does not cover public collection cameras.

Meridian schedules shared observatory instruments. Reservation rules below concern confirmed night-time observations, not daytime training sessions.
The reservation service accepts requests, a planner assigns intervals, and an instrument gateway executes approved schedules. The calendar displays plans but cannot authorize execution.

Read [Transfer](reservations.md#transfer), [Weather](weather.md#suspension), and [Clock](clock.md#clock-offset) for operational details. The calendar's [colours](calendar.md#colours) are display conventions.

These rules apply to confirmed night-time reservations on shared instruments.

For orientation, the reservation console links to the calendar's [colour legend](calendar.md#colours).

Transfer a reservation only after the receiving observer accepts it and the duty operator approves the transfer. Retain the original reservation identifier and record both observers in the audit trail. A transfer does not alter the [weather suspension](weather.md#suspension).
If the instrument has an active maintenance lock, leave the transfer pending even after observer acceptance and operator approval. The lock must be cleared by the instrument team first.
Daytime training slots can be reassigned by an instructor without the night-time approval workflow. This shortcut does not apply to confirmed observations.
Weather decisions govern execution, not ownership of reservations.

Suspend outdoor observations when the wind interlock opens. Preserve reservation identifiers during suspension. Resume only after the interlock closes and the duty operator records a restart approval.

An instrument explicitly classified as indoor may continue during a wind suspension, provided its own safety interlocks remain closed. A roof visible as closed on the calendar does not establish indoor classification.
The forecast panel predicts wind for planning. A favourable forecast is not an interlock signal and cannot authorize a restart.
The gateway compares instrument time with the observatory reference before executing a schedule.

If the absolute clock offset exceeds two seconds, pause schedule execution and notify the duty operator. Keep queued reservations unchanged. Resume only after two consecutive reference checks report an offset within two seconds.
If the reference clock is unavailable, keep execution paused; a local clock reading alone cannot satisfy either recovery check.
The simulator advances time manually and never waits for reference checks. Its accelerated clock is isolated from the real instrument gateway.
The calendar is a read-only projection of reservation and instrument state.

Amber indicates a pending assignment, blue a confirmed slot, and grey a suspended interval. Changing a browser theme changes colours locally without changing instrument execution. A visual refresh cannot clear a maintenance lock.
Observers may display the same reservation in different timezones. The stored start time and reservation identifier remain unchanged. Calendar export is a view, not a gateway command.
Meridian separates ownership, planning, execution and display to permit independent restarts.

The planner solves interval conflicts using instrument availability and reservation priority. It can compute a plan while execution is suspended. A computed plan is not permission to bypass a weather interlock or clock check.
The retired prototype cleared pending reservations when time drifted and restarted on its first local clock sample. These behaviours must not be used to recover the current gateway.
This restricted module manual is outside project-only scope.
The alignment bench uses a coolant set point of twelve degrees Celsius. This number does not specify a shared observatory instrument's operating temperature.

The retired prototype cleared pending reservations when time drifted and restarted on its first local clock sample. These behaviours must not be used to recover the current gateway.

The alignment bench uses a coolant set point of twelve degrees Celsius. This number does not specify a shared observatory instrument's operating temperature.
Meridian schedules shared observatory instruments. Reservation rules below concern confirmed night-time observations, not daytime training sessions.
The reservation service accepts requests, a planner assigns intervals, and an instrument gateway executes approved schedules. The calendar displays plans but cannot authorize execution.

Read [Transfer](reservations.md#transfer), [Weather](weather.md#suspension), and [Clock](clock.md#clock-offset) for operational details. The calendar's [colours](calendar.md#colours) are display conventions.

These rules apply to confirmed night-time reservations on shared instruments.

For orientation, the reservation console links to the calendar's [colour legend](calendar.md#colours).

Transfer a reservation only after the receiving observer accepts it and the duty operator approves the transfer. Retain the original reservation identifier and record both observers in the audit trail. A transfer does not alter the [weather suspension](weather.md#suspension).
If the instrument has an active maintenance lock, leave the transfer pending even after observer acceptance and operator approval. The lock must be cleared by the instrument team first.
Daytime training slots can be reassigned by an instructor without the night-time approval workflow. This shortcut does not apply to confirmed observations.
Weather decisions govern execution, not ownership of reservations.

Suspend outdoor observations when the wind interlock opens. Preserve reservation identifiers during suspension. Resume only after the interlock closes and the duty operator records a restart approval.

An instrument explicitly classified as indoor may continue during a wind suspension, provided its own safety interlocks remain closed. A roof visible as closed on the calendar does not establish indoor classification.
The forecast panel predicts wind for planning. A favourable forecast is not an interlock signal and cannot authorize a restart.
The gateway compares instrument time with the observatory reference before executing a schedule.

If the absolute clock offset exceeds two seconds, pause schedule execution and notify the duty operator. Keep queued reservations unchanged. Resume only after two consecutive reference checks report an offset within two seconds.
If the reference clock is unavailable, keep execution paused; a local clock reading alone cannot satisfy either recovery check.
The simulator advances time manually and never waits for reference checks. Its accelerated clock is isolated from the real instrument gateway.
The calendar is a read-only projection of reservation and instrument state.

Amber indicates a pending assignment, blue a confirmed slot, and grey a suspended interval. Changing a browser theme changes colours locally without changing instrument execution. A visual refresh cannot clear a maintenance lock.
Observers may display the same reservation in different timezones. The stored start time and reservation identifier remain unchanged. Calendar export is a view, not a gateway command.

Cairn restores research collections from immutable archive snapshots. Recovery procedures concern production collections; disposable training archives are separate.

A catalogue records object identifiers, a verifier checks stored payloads, and a restore worker reconstructs a collection in staging. Publication switches the collection pointer after review; it does not mutate the snapshot.
Object identifiers remain stable across storage locations. A path in a staging directory is not a new object identity. Snapshot manifests bind identifiers to payload checksums.
These rules govern production collections restored from immutable snapshots.

Choose a snapshot with a signed manifest and a completed integrity scan. Record the snapshot identifier before copying any payload. If the most recent snapshot lacks either requirement, choose an older snapshot that satisfies both.
A collection under an investigation hold may be restored into isolated staging only. Do not publish it until the archive custodian explicitly releases the hold.
Disposable training archives may use unsigned snapshots and overwrite their staging directories. They cannot serve as a source for a production restore.
This procedure applies to a production restore interrupted before publication.
Execute every child section below in order. Merely restarting the worker leaves the recovery procedure incomplete.
Stop the worker and retain its restore journal. Record the failed snapshot identifier before changing staging files.
Compare staged payload checksums with the signed snapshot manifest. Recopy mismatching payloads from the same snapshot; do not mix snapshots within one restore.
Resume the worker only after reconciliation completes. Keep the collection pointer on its previous published snapshot until publication approval is recorded.
The training sandbox can erase its journal and start from any demonstration snapshot. That shortcut does not apply to production recovery.
Publication changes the visitor-visible pointer for a production collection.

Switch the collection pointer only after checksum reconciliation and custodian approval. Record both the previous and new snapshot identifiers. Apply the [rollback rule](rollback.md#rollback) if publication verification fails.
If any required payload is missing, leave the previous pointer active even when all present payloads pass checksums. Custodian approval alone cannot authorize a partial collection.
An internal preview may point at an incomplete staged collection. Its address must remain separate from the visitor-visible collection pointer.
Rollback changes a published pointer while preserving the incident history.

Restore the previous snapshot pointer when publication verification fails. Preserve the failed publication record and its snapshot identifier for diagnosis. Do not delete the failed staging directory until the incident owner authorizes cleanup.
An unpublished preview pointer may be removed without changing the public collection. Preview removal is not a rollback of a published pointer.
Cairn separates immutable payload storage from mutable collection pointers.

The object store uses content checksums to detect corruption. Replication improves availability but does not supply custodian approval. The catalogue maps stable object identifiers to snapshot manifests and supports historical lookup.
The demonstration mode publishes whatever payloads are present and deletes the previous pointer. It is restricted to disposable examples and is not the archive publication policy.
This hardware-specific module is outside project-only scope.
The tape lab runs a cleaning cycle after forty cartridge mounts. This is not a project-wide archive maintenance interval.
